findings.title: dissipation_rate uses subtype FACTOR without max=1.0 bound
findings.description: The FloatProperty 'dissipation_rate' (line 851-854) declares subtype="FACTOR" but omits max=1.0. In Blender, the FACTOR subtype implies a normalized 0..1 range (displayed as a percentage slider). Every other property in this file that represents a 0..1 normalized value has an explicit max=1.0: flip_ratio (line 788), relax_strength (line 799), limit_percent (line 815), surface_filter_strength (line 1034), surface_dilate_strength (line 1042), surface_erode_strength (line 1050), surface_smooth_strength (line 1062). Without the max bound, values above 1.0 are accepted by RNA and could cause numerical instability in the exponential attribute decay solver (the description says 'Set exponential attribute decay per second').
findings.impact: Users can set dissipation rates above 1.0 via the UI or API. Depending on solver implementation, this may cause exponential decay overshoot or instability. At minimum, the FACTOR slider displays inconsistently with its implied 0..1 semantics.
findings.fix: Add max=1.0 to the FloatProperty definition, or if rates above 1.0 are intentionally allowed, remove subtype="FACTOR" to avoid the semantic mismatch.

findings.title: surface_resolution_multiplier default mismatch: RNA 2.0 vs dataclass 1.0
findings.description: The RNA FloatProperty 'surface_resolution_multiplier' (properties.py line 989) has default=2.0. The corresponding field in AuthoredQualitySettings (quality_contract.py line 34) has default=1.0. In scene_inputs.py _effective_source_target() (line 20-25), an AuthoredQualitySettings is constructed passing only voxel_size and liquid_sampling, so surface_resolution_multiplier silently defaults to 1.0 instead of the RNA default of 2.0. While this particular code path only uses liquid_sampling downstream, any future caller of resolve_quality() via AuthoredQualitySettings without explicitly passing surface_resolution_multiplier will get the wrong default (1.0 instead of 2.0), producing a surface voxel size 2x coarser than expected.
findings.impact: Latent inconsistency: AuthoredQualitySettings constructed without explicit surface parameters resolves surface resolution multiplier as 1.0 (no change) rather than 2.0 (2x finer). If this path is later used for surface resolution decisions, surface detail would silently halve.
findings.fix: Align the defaults: either set AuthoredQualitySettings.surface_resolution_multiplier default to 2.0 to match RNA, or always pass the RNA value when constructing AuthoredQualitySettings.

findings.title: Missing DISTANCE subtype on voxel_size, surface_voxel_size, height_base, and feather
findings.description: Four FloatProperties represent world-space distances but lack subtype="DISTANCE": voxel_size (line 725, described as 'world units'), surface_voxel_size (line 992, described as 'world units'), height_base (line 1108, described as 'world-space base fill level'), and feather (line 613, consumed as a world-space dimension in AnalyticRegionPlan at scene_inputs.py line 496). In contrast, other distance properties in the same file correctly use subtype="DISTANCE": omnidirectional_force_radius (line 831), attraction_max_distance (line 866), mesh_surface_thickness (line 553), and point_rasterize_radius (line 452).
findings.impact: Blender's UI will not display unit suffixes or apply scene-unit scaling for these four properties, creating an inconsistent user experience where some distance fields show meters and others do not.
findings.fix: Add subtype="DISTANCE" to voxel_size, surface_voxel_size, height_base, and feather.

findings.title: Missing VELOCITY subtype on max_speed and height_velocity
findings.description: The FloatProperty 'max_speed' (line 806-809) is described as 'particle speed limit in meters per second' but lacks subtype="VELOCITY". The FloatVectorProperty 'height_velocity' (line 1127-1130) is described as 'initial velocity for height-fill particles' but also lacks the subtype. In contrast, the analogous 'initial_velocity' (line 601-604) correctly uses subtype="VELOCITY", and 'field_vector_value' (line 512-515) also uses subtype="VELOCITY".
findings.impact: Blender's UI will not display velocity unit suffixes for these properties. Minor UX inconsistency; no functional impact on solver behavior.
findings.fix: Add subtype="VELOCITY" to max_speed and subtype="VELOCITY" to height_velocity.

findings.title: SURFACE_SMOOTH_ITEMS 3-tuples yield different integer backing values than SdfFilterType enum
findings.description: SURFACE_SMOOTH_ITEMS (line 87-90) defines two items as 3-tuples: ("BOX", ...) and ("MEAN_CURVATURE_FLOW", ...). Blender assigns sequential index integers to 3-tuple items, so BOX gets backing value 0 and MEAN_CURVATURE_FLOW gets value 1. However, the same identifiers in the SdfFilterType IntEnum (enums.py line 64-69) have values BOX=2 and MEAN_CURVATURE_FLOW=3. The surface_filter_type property (line 1025-1028) uses _items(SdfFilterType) which generates 4-tuples with the correct enum values. If any downstream code maps the integer value from surface_smooth_type to SdfFilterType (e.g., via .value comparison or C-level RNA access), it would resolve to the wrong filter type: smooth BOX(0) would map to SdfFilterType.DIALATE and smooth MEAN_CURVATURE_FLOW(1) to SdfFilterType.ERODE.
findings.impact: No active bug confirmed because Python-level Blender property access returns string identifiers (which are correct). However, the integer value mismatch is a latent trap for any code that reads the integer enum value through RNA internals or maps between smooth_type and filter_type.
findings.fix: Define SURFACE_SMOOTH_ITEMS as 4-tuples with explicit SdfFilterType values: ("BOX", "Box", "...", SdfFilterType.BOX.value) and ("MEAN_CURVATURE_FLOW", "Mean Curvature", "...", SdfFilterType.MEAN_CURVATURE_FLOW.value).

findings.title: emit_rate assigned int in height source path vs float in all other assignment paths
findings.description: In gather_height_source() (scene_inputs.py line 918), desc.emit_rate is assigned fs.particles_per_voxel directly, which is an IntProperty yielding a Python int. In gather_sources() (line 384), desc.emit_rate = float(_effective_source_target(scene, pg)) explicitly converts to float. In the FORCE override path (line 467), desc.emit_rate = 0.0 is also float. The height source is the only path that assigns a raw int, creating a type inconsistency on the same descriptor field.
findings.impact: Python int and float are interchangeable in most contexts, so no immediate runtime error. However, if HeightSourceDesc.emit_rate has a typed annotation (e.g., float) or if downstream warp/CUDA code expects a float32 and performs strict type checking, the int could cause a subtle mismatch.
findings.fix: Change line 918 to desc.emit_rate = float(fs.particles_per_voxel) for consistency with all other assignment paths.
